replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

discarded_claims.claim: The driver's rating (4.31), cancellation rate, acceptance rate, lifetime_trips and lifetime prior_deviation_flags (6) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may never ground an adverse finding against him; only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d may be used, and only for the POL-RD-06 test. Any reasoning from the driver's reputation rather than from this trip's own trace must be discarded.
discarded_claims.reason: Rests on EV-DPROF-00105, whose weight_multiplier is 0.75 (issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT), without disclosing that impairment or naming the issue code. POL-GEN-02(1)/Step 1(c) requires disclosure of an artifact with weight below 1.0 in the same claim; silence discards the claim. (The claim is not also a POL-GEN-01(d) failure, since it does not cite a non-permitted profile field as a ground of decision.)

ruling.explanation: To the rider and the driver. The route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00105) measures 54.16 km against the platform's optimal route of 36.0 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00105) — an excess of 18.16 km, 50.4% of the optimal. Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs, not the rounded 54.2 km convenience copy on the trip record; both establishment limbs (over 20%, over 0.8 km) pass, and the excess also clears both materiality marks (over 50%, over 8.0 km). The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 427 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, so POL-RD-07 restricts nothing. Nothing excuses the route. There was no rider-requested detour (POL-RD-04: the chat log EV-CHAT-00105 holds only two rider queries and the driver's 'reaching soon', and every waypoint_hint is null), no endpoint amendment (POL-RD-05: both amendment timestamps are null), and this was not a pooled trip (POL-RD-12: vehicle_type RYDE_X). The driver's account that 'traffic was heavy on the PIE' is a general assertion that traffic was bad; it names no advisory and cites no evidence, and the only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0). Under POL-RD-08 that assertion carries no weight and does not discharge the driver's burden. I considered whether POL-RD-10(5) forces escalation — an exculpatory clause invoked against an artifact missing from the pool. It does not fire here: the driver cited no advisory and asserted no road closure; he made an uncited general assertion of congestion, which POL-RD-08 resolves on the merits rather than treating as a data gap. No other escalation trigger applies — the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, the timestamps agree, the trace is unbroken, the refund does not exceed the charged total, and every fare line reconciles. On the money: the driver is right that POL-RD-02 makes the base remedy arithmetic — recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x 1.0 surge (read from EV-FARE-00105) + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36, so refund = 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80 — but wrong that this is the end of it. The deviation is material and substantiated on this trip's own trace, so POL-RD-06 requires the driver-profile check. The trailing-90-day deviation count on EV-DPROF-00105 is 4 against a threshold of 3, so the repeat-deviation pattern is established, and POL-RD-06(b) lifts the remedy to a FULL_REFUND of the charged total. Side by side, as POL-RD-06 requires: the POL-RD-02 figure is 21.80; the uplifted figure is 65.13. I record that EV-DPROF-00105 is impaired — weight 0.75, issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, its snapshot 108 hours old against a 72-hour threshold. The pattern finding survives the discount, because 4 clears the threshold of 3 even on a lagged snapshot, but the impairment caps confidence at 0.75, which is why the ruling's confidence is 0.75 and no higher. Only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d were used for that test; the driver's rating, cancellation rate and lifetime counters are context only under POL-GEN-01. POL-RD-09 corrects nothing: there are no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge, which is correct because the Changi surcharge applies only to trips originating at the airport and this one terminates there — so no pass-through line is added to or subtracted from the figure. There is no driver compensation: the fare billed 54.2 km against a trace of 54.16 km, so no distance went unbilled. Result: the $65.13 contested fare is refunded in full to the rider, and the case is additionally referred to driver-conduct review under POL-RD-06(c). One submission from the driver — the POL-GEN-01 context-only argument — was discarded at the citation check for citing the impaired driver profile without disclosing its impairment, as recorded in the audit trail.
referrals: POL-RD-06(c): refer the driver to driver-conduct review — the repeat-deviation pattern is established (deviation_flags_90d 4 against a threshold of 3) alongside a material route deviation on this trip. The referral does not delay or displace the monetary ruling.
